description: Single-panel figure consisting of a text table rather than a plot. It reports Mössbauer spectroscopy hyperfine parameters of Fe-Al ferritic low-density steels together with the atomic configurations assigned to each magnetic hyperfine field. The five columns are Composition, B_hf (T) (± 0.5 T), Area (%) (± 1%), V_f (%) (± 1%), and Assignment (atomic configurations). Five compositions are tabulated: the α-Fe-foil reference plus Fe-5Al, Fe-6Al, Fe-6.8Al and Fe-9Al. α-Fe-foil occupies one row, B_hf = 33 T, Area 100%, V_f 100%, assigned (8Fe)nn + (6Fe)nnn. Adding Al splits the spectrum into more components: Fe-5Al has two rows (32.67 and 30.65 T), Fe-6Al four, Fe-6.8Al five, and Fe-9Al eight. In every alloy the highest-field component (about 30.3-30.65 T) dominates with the largest Area and V_f, while components below 26 T stay small. Area (%) and V_f (%) track each other closely for every row, consistent with spectral area being proportional to volume fraction of the corresponding atomic configuration; progressively Al-richer near-neighbour configurations such as (5Fe+3Al)nn and (4Fe+4Al)nn appear only at higher Al content.

observations.observation: The figure is a single tabular image whose five column headers are Composition, B_hf (T) (± 0.5 T), Area (%) (± 1%), V_f (%) (± 1%), and Assignment (atomic configurations).
The α-Fe-foil reference is listed with a single component: B_hf = 33 T, Area = 100%, V_f = 100%, assigned (8Fe)nn + (6Fe)nnn.
Fe-5Al is fitted with two components: B_hf = 32.67 T (Area 24%, V_f 23.55%) and 30.65 T (Area 51.6%, V_f 50.7%).
The number of fitted hyperfine-field components grows with Al content: 1 for α-Fe-foil, 2 for Fe-5Al, 4 for Fe-6Al, 5 for Fe-6.8Al and 8 for Fe-9Al.
In each Fe-Al alloy the component with the largest Area and V_f lies near 30.3-30.65 T; e.g. in Fe-9Al the 30.31 T row has Area 44.1% and V_f 42.3%.
Components with B_hf below 26 T remain minor, the largest being the 25.48 T row of Fe-9Al with Area 17.5% and V_f 18.9%.
Area (%) and V_f (%) are numerically very close for every row, consistent with spectral area being proportional to the volume fraction of the corresponding atomic configuration.
The assignment (4Fe+4Al)nn + (6Fe)nnn appears only at 23.26 T in Fe-6.8Al and at 23.31 T and 22.97 T in Fe-9Al.
The assignment (7Fe+1Al)nn + (6Fe)nnn Or (8Fe)nn + (6Al)nnn is the dominant component in all four Fe-Al alloys (Area about 44-54%, V_f about 42-53.5%).
In Fe-9Al the 27.54 T row is uniquely assigned (6Fe+2Al)nn + (4Fe+2Al)nnn, differing from the (6Fe+2Al)nn + (6Fe)nnn assignment given to the same field region in Fe-6Al and Fe-6.8Al.

The caption states the table lists the hyperfine magnetic field (B_hf), spectral area, volume fraction (V_f) and the proposed assignments of the atomic configurations that produce each respective magnetic hyperfine field.
